ideas.title: Heave! The friends push the empty cart up the dune
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: This breaks the long run of devices left alone under a fixed camera: creatures put real force into a rigid body that sinks and ruts in the sand field, and the player gets a timing skill to learn. The risk is the friends' 'pushing': if their feet don't really slip and dig, and the cart's lurch is tuned until it lands on 'two on planks, four in sand', it becomes a rig made for one case.

ideas.title: The friends carry the planks
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A procession of creatures hauling things is a cozy-game staple, and the payoff (slower walk, crooked planks) is mostly logistics. Load set by mass ratio is honest, but 'sway that follows the gait' tends to become a parented prop that wobbles, with no body really holding anything.

ideas.title: The cart creaks: sound from the physics
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Sound synthesised from stick-slip and compaction is something the island has never done, and greasing the axle to make it quiet is a nice thing to hear. But it depends on a cart that doesn't exist yet, and without one it is a sound technique with nothing to play.

ideas.title: Wind that moves the dune overnight
ideas.nearest: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Saltation and lee-side slumping on the GPU, with the dune reshaped every morning, is new physics and a real daily rhythm, and it is the strongest radical pitch here. The danger is that overnight change is invisible while it happens; if nobody can watch the streamers and slip faces work, it reads as a terrain swap.

ideas.title: My body learns to carry
ideas.critique: A balance controller driven by real torque is real animation work and serves the self and motion goals. But a creature straining under a load is an expected character beat, and handing Lumi things has little goal past watching it cope.

ideas.title: Braking down the far side
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A descent you can lose either way is a genuinely playable skill, and riders sliding by real deceleration is honest. It is built on a cart and a climb that don't exist yet, so as this session's step it shows nothing on its own.

ideas.title: Two gauges on one road
ideas.critique: A second, smaller cart and a race is one more prop and an event, and the gauge-matching mechanic boils down to a single check of whether a wheel is on a plank. It is the most predictable idea of the round.

ideas.title: The windmill turns my motor backwards
ideas.critique: It is a genuine road step and joins cloth, wind, the motor and circuit.jl into one chain, but its payoff is a glowing wire on the bench, the very image of 'Where I rushed it', filmed as one more device at dusk. Setting sail area against gusts is a choice, though a thin one.

ideas.title: Lead plates that fizz
ideas.critique: It is the core of the storage step, and plates whose colour and capacity build up over days are an honest mechanism. Yet it is another vessel of liquid changing colour on its own under a close camera, the island's most worn recipe, and forming a plate over days is waiting rather than play.

ideas.title: A sand dune race the friends invent
ideas.critique: Creatures taking up a tool as play, choosing roles by mass and tiring by the real work done, speaks to the interactions goal. It needs the cart first, and role-swapping behaviour easily becomes a scripted loop that only looks emergent.
